challenge_facts_addressed.effect_on_judgment: The two one-on-one initiations provide some support for special interest, but both occurred in class or project-related contexts, and LB-F4 shows that Alex also makes one-on-one plans with at least four other friends.

Remembering the presentation and sending encouragement could reflect personal attentiveness, but the presentation was listed in the group calendar and the tea was brought for the whole group, limiting evidence that Jordan was singled out.

The extended message exchanges show willingness to engage with Jordan, but their occurrence after group events and their mostly class- and group-related content do not clearly indicate special or romantic interest.

reason_for_retaining_or_changing: Interpretation B remains better supported. LB-F1 through LB-F3 show friendly attention and some one-on-one engagement, but they are context-bound and not clearly exclusive. LB-F4 establishes similar behavior toward others, while LB-F5 and LB-F6 more directly weigh against romantic interest by showing Alex offering to introduce Jordan to someone else and redirecting a proposed one-on-one dinner into a group dinner.

revised_recommended_action.explanation: Treat Alex's behavior as general friendliness unless clearer evidence emerges, while continuing the existing level of interaction without assuming romantic interest.
